summary: Ferdinand Sommer was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Marburg, Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen, and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and Eduard Sievers. He held professorships at Basel (1902), Rostock (1909–1913), Jena (1913–1924), Bonn (1924–1926), and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Geneva, Berlin, and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Karl Brugmann, and Georg Curtius. He served as Maître de Conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1881–1891) and professor at Geneva (1891–1913).

Ferdinand von Eckstein worked in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at Heidelberg under Friedrich Creuzer and at Göttingen. He was a member of the Société Asiatique (~1822–1861) and founded Le Catholique in 1826.

Ferdinand von Richthofen was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Breslau (~1850–1853) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1856). He held posts at Bonn (~1875–1883), Leipzig (~1883–1886), and Berlin (~1886–1905).

Ferdinando Belloni-Filippi worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Pisa under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè and Carlo Formichi, and at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Pisa, Bologna (1910), and the University of Florence (1919–1952).

Ferenc Ruzsa works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium and Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982), where he served as Kari munkatárs (~1982) and assistant professor of metaphysics (~1993–2010).

Fernand Brunner was a philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Lausanne (~1938–1942) and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Paris (~1946–1951). He served as professor at Neuchâtel (1954–1986) and taught at Bern (1956–1985).

Fernand Grenard worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Sciences Po (École Libre des Sciences Politiques) from ~1887 to 1889 and at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from ~1887 to 1890.

Fernand Meyer specializes in Tibetology. He held posts at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique, the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2004), and the Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research (2016).
Fernando Jose Benetti works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University, completing his doctoral research under Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying at the National University of San Marcos. He served as professor at the University of Buenos Aires (~1970–2000) and was director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).
Fernando Wulff works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held a post at the University of Málaga around 1989.
Filip Rucinski works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 2000 to 2006 and completed an M.A. at the University of Warsaw in 2009.

Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Moscow State, Tübingen, Berlin, Leipzig, and Paris under scholars including Roth, Weber, Curtius, and Bréal. He served as professor at Moscow State University (1875–1886) and joined the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Filippo De Filippi was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.

Filippo Marsili works in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, Arcangela Santoro, and Paolo Daffinà. He was attested at Saint Louis University in 2019.

Finnian McKean Moore Gerety specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard (2007–2015) under Michael Witzel, held a postdoc at Yale (2017–2018), and was a Visiting Assistant Professor at Brown (2018–2024), also holding posts at Oxford.

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He held professorships at Government College University, Lahore, Sanskrit College and University, and King's College London, and was Librarian at the India Office (1864–1869).

Flavio Geisshuesler works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Lausanne, Bern, and the University of Virginia under David Germano, holding posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2019) and the University of Sydney (2023).
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas between ~1978 and 1983, and taught Jacques Giès.
